final_message:
We had a bit of excitement at our house this week, and I must tell you of it before the news gets stale.

You know that our old hen, Mrs. Biddy, has been setting on a nest behind the woodpile since the first of the month. We had given her up as a hopeless case, for she refused to be moved, and the rooster went about for days with the look of a man who has been wronged. Mr. Stewart declared she was only sulking and would never hatch a thing. "She's a daft auld bird," he said, "and ye'll see naught come of it." Well, on Tuesday morning there was a great peeping, and out from under her marched seven yellow chicks, as pert as you please. Mr. Stewart took off his hat and looked at them a long while, and then said, "Mayhap I was hasty."

The next piece of news is that our eldest boy, Robert, has taken a position at the mill in town. He is to go in on Monday and will board with the Hendersons through the week, coming home on Saturday nights. He is very proud, and has been polishing his shoes since Wednesday, though they were fairly bright to begin with. I am glad for him, but I confess the house will seem quiet. He is the one who whistles over his chores, and I have grown so used to it that I shall miss it sorely. I have packed him two clean shirts, a jar of plum butter, and a good deal of advice, which he received with great patience and I suspect has already forgotten.

Little Annie lost her first tooth on Thursday. She came running in from the yard holding it up in her fingers, and the front of her was a perfect sight, for she had been crying and laughing at the same time. We put it under her pillow, and Mr. Stewart, who is a very resourceful man, left a bright new nickel in its place. In the morning she was sure the fairy had been kept awake all night by the dog barking, and she felt dreadfully sorry for her.

The weather has turned cold, with a hard frost on the pump handle each morning, and we have begun to burn the stove all day. The apples are in the cellar and the last of the corn is in the crib. I think we are as ready for winter as we are likely to be.

Write soon and tell me how your folks are getting on. I have so wanted to hear.
